```{r}
#| echo: false
#| message: false
#| warning: false

library(officer.pptx)
knitr::opts_chunk$set(
  collapse = TRUE,
  comment = "#>"
)

image_insert_thumbnail <- function(name) {
  vapply(name, function(one_name) {
    source_candidates <- c(
      file.path("inst/ext/vignettes/image-insert-thumbnails", one_name),
      file.path("..", "inst/ext/vignettes/image-insert-thumbnails", one_name),
      system.file(
        "ext/vignettes/image-insert-thumbnails",
        one_name,
        package = "officer.pptx"
      )
    )
    source_path <- source_candidates[file.exists(source_candidates)][1]
    if (is.na(source_path)) {
      stop("Thumbnail not found: ", one_name, call. = FALSE)
    }
    local_dir <- "image-insert-thumbnails"
    dir.create(local_dir, showWarnings = FALSE)
    local_path <- file.path(local_dir, one_name)
    file.copy(source_path, local_path, overwrite = TRUE)
    local_path
  }, character(1))
}
```

## Introduction

`image_insert()` places images over existing slide shapes that act as position
markers. This is useful when a template deck contains manually positioned
rectangles with marker text like `{photo}` or `{chart_1}`, and you want to fill
those positions programmatically at report-generation time.

The function builds on `shape_select()` and reuses the same frame-fitting logic
as `img()`. The key difference is:
 
- `img()` places images into officer **placeholders** (layout-defined content
  areas).
- `image_insert()` places images over arbitrary **shapes** already present on
  the slide.

## Quick Start

The following example creates a slide with two marker shapes, then inserts an
image over each marker:

```{r}
#| eval: false
library(officer.pptx)

x <- read_pptx("template.pptx")

x <- image_insert(
  x,
  image = "photo.png",
  pattern = "{photo}",
  fit = "inside"
)

print(x, target = "output.pptx")
```

This finds every shape whose visible text contains `"{photo}"` and inserts
`photo.png` fitted inside that shape's bounding box.

**Before** -- two marker shapes on a blank slide:

```{r}
#| echo: false
#| out-width: "70%"

knitr::include_graphics(image_insert_thumbnail("thumb-before.png"))
```

**After** `image_insert()` with `fit = "inside"`:

```{r}
#| echo: false
#| out-width: "70%"

knitr::include_graphics(image_insert_thumbnail("thumb-after-inside.png"))
```

**After** with `fit = "fill"` (stretches to fill the marker exactly):

```{r}
#| echo: false
#| out-width: "70%"

knitr::include_graphics(image_insert_thumbnail("thumb-after-fill.png"))
```

**After** hiding the markers with `shape_update(hidden = TRUE)`:

```{r}
#| echo: false
#| out-width: "70%"

knitr::include_graphics(image_insert_thumbnail("thumb-after-hidden.png"))
```

## Target Selection

### Pattern mode

The simplest approach uses `pattern` to search shape text:

```{r}
#| eval: false
x <- image_insert(x, image = "logo.png", pattern = "{logo}")
```

By default `fixed = TRUE`, which means substring matching (no regex). Set
`fixed = FALSE` for regular expression matching:

```{r}
#| eval: false
x <- image_insert(x, image = "chart.png", pattern = "\\{chart_\\d+\\}", fixed = FALSE)
```

Use `slide_idx` to restrict the search to specific slides:

```{r}
#| eval: false
x <- image_insert(x, image = "chart.png", pattern = "{chart}", slide_idx = c(2, 4))
```

### Selection mode

For more control, first select targets with `shape_select()` and pass the result:

```{r}
#| eval: false
targets <- shape_select(x, text = "{photo}", match = "exact", kind = "shape")
x <- image_insert(x, image = "photo.png", selection = targets)
```

This lets you use the full `shape_select()` filter set: text, name, kind, slide,
placeholder status, hidden flag, and matching mode.

### Pipeline mode

Selections can also be piped directly:

```{r}
#| eval: false
x <- shape_select(x, text = "{photo}", match = "exact") |>
  image_insert(image = "photo.png", fit = "fill")
```

## Image Fitting

The `fit` parameter controls how the image is sized relative to the target shape:

| `fit`      | Behavior                                                       |
|------------|----------------------------------------------------------------|
| `"inside"` | Scale to fit entirely inside the target (default)              |
| `"outside"`| Scale to cover the target completely                           |
| `"width"`  | Match target width; height adjusts proportionally              |
| `"height"` | Match target height; width adjusts proportionally              |
| `"fill"`   | Stretch to fill the exact target dimensions (may distort)      |
| `"none"`   | Use the image's raw dimensions without scaling                 |

After fitting, you can further adjust with `scale`:

```{r}
#| eval: false
x <- image_insert(x, image = "icon.png", pattern = "{icon}", fit = "inside", scale = 0.8)
```

## Positioning

### Justification

Use `h_just` and `v_just` to control alignment within the target frame:

- `h_just`: 0 = left, 0.5 = center (default), 1 = right
- `v_just`: 0 = bottom, 0.5 = center (default), 1 = top

```{r}
#| eval: false
x <- image_insert(x, "photo.png", pattern = "{photo}", h_just = 0, v_just = 1)
```

### Offsets

Use `x_offset` and `y_offset` to shift the image after fitting:

```{r}
#| eval: false
x <- image_insert(x, "photo.png", pattern = "{photo}", x_offset = 0.1, y_offset = -0.05)
```
 
The `offset_mode` parameter controls the unit:

| `offset_mode` | Meaning                                          |
|---------------|--------------------------------------------------|
| `"source"`    | Multiple of the scaled image width/height        |
| `"target"`    | Multiple of the target shape width/height        |
| `"units"`     | Raw inches                                       |

## Vectorization

Multiple images can be inserted in one call. `image` and `pattern` must have
length one or a common length:

```{r}
#| eval: false
x <- image_insert(
  x,
  image = c("photo_1.png", "photo_2.png"),
  pattern = c("{photo_1}", "{photo_2}"),
  fit = "inside"
)
```

Each pattern may match multiple shapes; the corresponding image is inserted over
every match.

In selection mode, `image` must have length one (same image for all targets) or
one value per row:
 
```{r}
#| eval: false
targets <- shape_select(x, text = "\\{photo_\\d+\\}", match = "regex")
x <- image_insert(x, image = rep("fallback.png", nrow(targets)), selection = targets)
```

## Hiding Markers

The original marker shape is kept in place. If you want to hide it after
inserting the image, use `shape_update()`:

```{r}
#| eval: false
targets <- shape_select(x, text = "{photo}", match = "exact")
x <- image_insert(x, image = "photo.png", selection = targets)
x <- shape_update(x, targets, hidden = TRUE)
```

## Empty Selection Handling

By default, `image_insert()` errors when no target shape is found:

```{r}
#| eval: false
x <- image_insert(x, image = "photo.png", pattern = "{missing}")
#> Error: No shape matched `pattern` "{missing}".
```

Use `empty = "ignore"` to silently skip when nothing matches:

```{r}
#| eval: false
x <- image_insert(x, image = "photo.png", pattern = "{optional}", empty = "ignore")
```

## Limitations

- Only **top-level** slide objects are selectable. Shapes inside groups are not
  matched.
- The image is fitted to the **rectangular bounding box**. Nonrectangular shapes
  (e.g., circles, arrows) do not clip the image.
- Target rotation is not inherited by the inserted image.
- `fit = "outside"` makes the image larger than the target without cropping.
- Placeholder shapes (from layouts) are explicitly rejected; use `img()` with
  `ph_with()` for those.

## Comparison with `img()`

| Feature              | `img()`                        | `image_insert()`                   |
|----------------------|--------------------------------|------------------------------------|
| Target               | Layout placeholder             | Any existing slide shape           |
| Selection            | `ph_location_*()`              | `pattern` or `shape_select()`      |
| Insertion            | `ph_with(x, img(...), loc)`    | `image_insert(x, image, ...)`      |
| Fitting              | Same fitting engine            | Same fitting engine                |
| Styling (bg, line)   | Yes                            | Not yet                            |
| Rotation             | Yes                            | Not yet                            |

Both functions share the same frame-fitting logic (`frame_fit_to_target()`), so
`fit`, `scale`, `h_just`, `v_just`, `x_offset`, `y_offset`, and `offset_mode`
work identically.
